claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy has a lamellar microstructure.
The duplex microstructure contains a soft, ductile FCC phase and a hard B2 phase.
A rapid, single-step anneal can fully recrystallize the FCC phase while preserving the morphology and continuity of the B2 framework.
Moderate pre-deformation creates different strain levels in the FCC and B2 phases, allowing subsequent FCC recrystallization while the B2 phase only recovers.
The resulting microstructure consists of fully recrystallized, fine-grained FCC regions embedded in an intact, coarse B2 skeleton.
The FCC and B2 phases exhibit different recovery and recrystallization responses during deformation and subsequent annealing.
The FCC phase selectively recrystallizes because it has higher stored strain energy and a lower recrystallization barrier than B2.
Rapid heating limits coarsening or transformation of the B2 phase.
Phase-selective recrystallization modifies strain partitioning and releases the strain-hardening capacity of the duplex phases.
The enhanced strain partitioning and strain hardening simultaneously improve strength and ductility.
The treatment increases yield strength relative to conventional processing.
The treatment significantly improves uniform elongation relative to conventional processing.
A phase-selectively recrystallized EHEA can reach a strength level around 2 GPa.
A phase-selectively recrystallized EHEA can reach approximately 30–35% uniform elongation.
Conventionally processed eutectic alloys generally exhibit a trade-off between high strength and limited ductility.
The benefit requires sufficient pre-deformation and an annealing condition that fully recrystallizes FCC without detrimental B2 coarsening.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration can negate the mechanical-property benefit.
The magnitude of improvement depends sensitively on annealing parameters and alloy chemistry.
Scale-up and reproducibility of the rapid annealing treatment across manufacturing settings remain unvalidated.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis conditions the effect on sufficient pre-deformation, but the experiment permits as-cast samples and would treat failure in that potentially out-of-boundary state as falsification.
